description: r11 Panel-2 ALL-CORE (20-core) CPU baseline on GB10. Additive file; SPEED_NUMBERS_R11.json is unchanged. All timings below were taken in one clean window with the 720p render process group paused (SIGSTOP), GPU re-timed in the same window.
clean_window: 2026-11-09 04:46:04-04:47:11 PST (20:46:04-20:47:11 Taipei); render pgid 3750532 SIGSTOPed then SIGCONT (verified resumed: frame f_00009 written 04:47:24 PST)

machine.lscpu: 20 CPUs: 10x Cortex-X925 (max 3.9 GHz) + 10x Cortex-A725 (max 2.808 GHz), 1 thread/core, 1 NUMA node; nproc=20

method:
r11 panel-2 ALL-CORE CPU baseline (20 cores: 10 Cortex-X925 + 10 Cortex-A725 on GB10).
Same fp64 Warp CPU code path as speed_bench.py. Warp's 'cpu' device runs a launch on one thread, so we
use 20 worker processes, each pinned to one distinct core (os.sched_setaffinity), each running the Warp CPU kernel.
 - mc:    the UNMODIFIED gpu_core.mc kernel, launched per chunk on row-slices of the identical 1,048,576x14 draw array (seed 20261107).
 - sweep: gpu_core.sweep body is index-based (i = wp.tid()), so a chunk wrapper kernel 'sweep_off' is the verbatim sweep
          body with i = wp.tid() + offset and out[i - offset] written to a chunk view; every physics call is the same
          gpu_core @wp.func (temperatures, mass, radiator_mass).
Work distribution: dynamic (shared atomic chunk counter, CHUNK rows per grab) so the slower A725 cores don't bottleneck.
Timing: per repetition a fresh process pool; each worker does Warp init, module load and a 512-thread warm-up launch
(JIT excluded, like the baseline), then waits at a barrier. Timed window = barrier release -> last worker finished its last
chunk (time.perf_counter = CLOCK_MONOTONIC, system-wide). Results are written straight into shared memory (no copy).
Setup, process spawn, warm-up and post-processing excluded, as in the 1-core/GPU baseline. Median of 3 repetitions.
Verification: outputs compared element-wise vs. the GPU (cuda:0) and 1-core Warp-CPU outputs of the same kernels.
discarded: An earlier pass 04:36:41-04:37:44 PST ran while a render was active; it is not used (kept on GB10 in allcore/out/ for audit).

sweep.output_check: 20-core output bitwise identical to 1-core Warp CPU output (max abs diff 0.0) in all 3 reps, no NaN; 20-core vs GPU max abs diff 1.82e-12 (max rel 6.1e-16), identical to 1-core vs GPU; hard_feasible 3048, design_feasible 2347, selected_index 1037888 unchanged

mc.output_check: 20-core output bitwise identical to 1-core Warp CPU output (max abs diff 0.0) in all 3 reps, no NaN; 20-core vs GPU max abs diff 1.42e-10 (max rel 2.7e-10), identical to 1-core vs GPU; P(inlet<=393 K)=0.416625 unchanged

caveats: Warp device=cpu is single-threaded per launch; the 20-core baseline uses 20 pinned processes each running the Warp CPU kernel on dynamically claimed 8,192-row chunks. A hand-vectorised/SVE-tuned or OpenMP C++ CPU code could be faster; this is the same-code all-core baseline, not a best-possible CPU implementation.
Sweep uses a chunk wrapper kernel (verbatim sweep body with an index offset); MC uses the unmodified mc kernel on row slices.
Timing excludes process spawn, Warp init/JIT and warm-up, the same as the 1-core/GPU baseline excludes JIT/setup; includes per-chunk launch overhead and dynamic scheduling.
Cores 5-9 and 15-19 (X925) did ~2x the chunks of cores 0-4 and 10-14 (A725). Per-design X925 throughput in the 20-core run (3.95 us) matches the 1-core baseline (3.89 us), so there was no contention.
GPU rep 1 of the sweep (0.239 s) was slower than reps 2-3 (0.213 s), likely draining in-flight GPU work from the just-paused render; the median is unaffected.
